scope.signature_policy: The generated NumPy inventory freezes the oracle signatures. Raptors supports the numeric CPU forms implemented in the extension; device/like dispatch and specialized dtype variants stay with their owning later releases.

known_gaps: This is an implementation contract, not a release-candidate claim: full signature, warning/error-precedence, dtype, and aliasing closure is still in progress.

isclose/allclose use the native long-double bridge on targets where long double exceeds float64. Two focused precision cases skip on this macOS ARM64 host because its NumPy long double has no extra mantissa bits; hosted Linux x86-64 CPython 3.12-3.14 preview and wheel suites pass on a native extended-precision target.
Ordering accepts NumPy's numeric kinds but does not promise identical internal permutations for partition/argpartition or algorithm-specific sort kinds where NumPy leaves ordering unspecified.
Public methods and routines outside the frozen 0.4 inventory remain owned by 0.5-0.8 as documented in the roadmap.
known_limits: Inputs are numeric Raptors arrays and supported Python numeric values; third-party dispatch, like=, foreign buffers, and specialized dtype families are outside 0.4.

On candidate 0a5bfd5, the designated ARM64 host measures column normalization at 0.388x, grouped counting at 0.386x, and assembly/reordering at 0.906x (95% CI 0.854-0.988). Linux x86-64 measures 0.429x, 0.731x, and 1.072x respectively (assembly 95% CI 1.038-1.088). The assembly median misses the 0.80 target on both hosts, so the three-workflow performance gate remains pending.
The implementation is still based on scalar/native storage walkers in several routines; temporary-memory and allocation profiles must be measured before release.

cross_phase_generated_sequences.behavior: Deterministic generated cases retain a reversed/stepped 0.2 view through assignment and owner destruction, then compose a 0.3 modulo ufunc with 0.4 concatenation, sorting, and reduction; every result is compared with NumPy.

focused_differential.command: uv run --project raptors-python --extra dev --no-sync python -m pytest raptors-python/tests/preview/test_ufunc_differential.py raptors-python/tests/preview/test_routines.py -q

full_python_regression.command: uv run --project raptors-python --extra dev --no-sync python -m pytest raptors-python/tests/preview -q

atleast_identity_and_view_contract.behavior: Sufficient-rank Raptors arrays preserve Python identity; rank increases match NumPy shape, dtype, strides, flags, values, and write-through storage sharing, including scalar stride layout.

copyto_where_none.behavior: An explicit where=None is a false mask; an omitted where remains an unmasked copy.

cargo_workspace_tests.parallel_rerun_anomaly: One default-parallel workspace rerun exited with SIGTRAP in raptors-core einsum_test; the isolated target and three immediate default-parallel reruns passed.

clippy.command: cargo clippy --locked --offline -p raptors-longdouble -p raptors-storage -p raptors-python --all-targets -- -D warnings

signature_audit.command: inspect.signature over frozen Phase 0.4 top-level routines and ndarray methods, compared with compat/numpy-api-2.5.3.json
signature_audit.note: Parameter order/kinds across all 127 top-level routines and exact signatures across all 26 ndarray methods are checked. The remaining 28 top-level differences are limited to documented hidden-default objects and eye's dtype=float default; sort/argsort axis and ddof type now reflect NumPy's defaults. Routine-specific explicit-default behavior, warning/error, and error-precedence review remains open.

signature_default_refinements.command: uv run --project raptors-python --no-sync pytest raptors-python/tests/preview/test_routines.py -q -k 'ddof_signature or default_signatures'
signature_default_refinements.behavior: Top-level sort/argsort inspect axis=-1, and std/var/nanstd/nanvar inspect the integer ddof=0 default; omitted and explicit ddof=1 calls match NumPy. The 28 top-level entries remain signature mismatches due to the documented defaults.

top_level_signature_shape_audit.behavior: All 127 contracted top-level signatures have matching parameter order and kinds; only the exact 28 documented defaults differ, and every permitted difference is checked against its frozen sentinel/default category. All 26 ndarray method signatures match NumPy exactly.

passed_jobs: Safe storage and binding Rust checks

contiguous_float32_snapshot_and_fortran_.behavior: Native C-contiguous float32 snapshots use a bounds-validated byte-slice path; Fortran-row int32 sort gathers and writes checked byte slices, retaining the generic byte-order and layout fallbacks. The frozen workflow report records the measured result.

repeated_fortran_int32_concatenation.behavior: Repeated, identical Fortran-contiguous int32 views concatenated on axis 0 are copied directly into allocated byte storage without zero-initializing an output buffer; tests cover two and three inputs, multidimensional trailing blocks, source non-aliasing, and layout.

explicit_where_and_default_signatures.behavior: copyto accepts positional or keyword where with NumPy-compatible inspection; ndarray all/any expose keyword-only where and reject a positional mask.

extension_alias_lifetime_focused.command: uv run --project raptors-python --extra dev --no-sync python -m pytest raptors-python/tests/preview/test_routines.py -q

passed_jobs: Safe storage and binding Rust checks

extended_precision_linux_x86_64.result: Linux x86-64 exposes extra long-double mantissa bits; the full preview suite passed on every hosted CPython version, exercising the extended-precision differential cases skipped on macOS ARM64.

evidence.sanitizer_miri_and_alias_lifetime_gates: candidate_0a5bfd5 hosted CI and build-only release workflows passed Miri and AddressSanitizer; all eight stable-ABI wheel and clean-install targets passed with PyPI publication skipped; broader extension alias-lifetime audit remains pending

common_operation_guardrail.coverage_limit: This checks inherited ufunc/reduction cells only; Phase 0.4 creation, shape, joining, selection, ordering, and histogram operations are not yet covered by the common-operation matrix.

cross_architecture_performance.target: GitHub Actions Linux x86-64, CPython 3.14.3, release extension
